_comment: Cross-engine parity scene: blur-fill effect applied to a single image clip.
The output fills the frame with a blurred, scaled background plus a sharp foreground.
NOTE: The current golden hash (ff7f3f0f07030000) is identical to plain blur and other
effect scenes because the test fixture image (image/image.jpg) is a smooth vertical
gradient (R=254, G: 0->234, B=0) at 320x240. On such a gradient:
1. Blur barely changes block averages (no high-frequency detail to blur).
2. The image and frame share the same 4:3 aspect ratio, so cover-fit and contain-fit
produce identical layouts — the blurred background is fully occluded by the foreground.
3. The dim/tint (0.7/0.2) is too subtle for the color signature to distinguish.
To make this scene effective, either use a frame with a different aspect ratio (e.g. 16:9)
or replace the fixture image with one that has high-frequency detail.
